name: Weeknight Paella
description: Adam Ragusea's streamlined, small-batch Valencian-style paella with chicken wings and green beans.
recipeIngredient: 1 sweet pepper (small; or half a bell pepper)
1 cup paella rice (or other short-grain rice)

recipeInstructions.text: Toast saffron dry in a paella pan or 10-inch skillet over medium heat until fragrant, 1 minute. Crush it into a microwave-safe jug, add white wine and water, heat until hot, and let it steep.
Oil the pan with olive oil and heat over medium-high. Season chicken wings generously with salt and black pepper, then brown on all sides until nearly cooked through, 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, mince garlic and shallot, dice sweet pepper, and trim and halve a handful of green beans.

Push the wings to the edge of the pan. Cook the garlic, shallot, and pepper in the middle until soft and lightly golden. Stir in tomato paste and cook 1 minute, then add the green beans and cook 2 minutes.

Pour in the saffron liquid and salt it until it tastes slightly saltier than you'd like, since the rice will absorb it. Scatter in paella rice, spread it evenly, and reduce to a high simmer. Don't stir again. Sprinkle water over any spots that dry out before the rice is tender, 18-20 minutes.
When the rice is nearly done, raise the heat to brown the bottom into a crust. Pull it off the heat when you first smell toasting, 1-2 minutes.
Rest at least 15 minutes. Cut a lemon into wedges. Serve with a wide spoon, scraping up the crust, and squeeze lemon over at the table.

Swap the wings for a drained can of lima beans for a vegetarian version, and use smoked or sweet paprika (1 tsp) if you have no saffron. Good additions: butter beans, a rosemary sprig laid on top for the last few minutes, or shrimp and mussels pushed into the rice for the last 5–8 minutes.
